newsitem.title: INDIA: New Kashmir chief orders release of separatists.
newsitem.headline: New Kashmir chief orders release of separatists.

text.p: The new chief of India's troubled Jammu and Kashmir state on Thursday ordered the release of leading separatist leaders arrested last month.

"The Chief Minister Dr Farooq Abdullah has ordered that all leaders of Hurriyat Conference and Shabir Shah who were arrested during their anti-election campaign be released," a government statement said.

The All Parties Hurriyat (Freedom) Conference, a 30-party umbrella organisation of separatist groups, had called for a boycott of recent state assembly elections in which Abdullah's National Conference party won a sweeping victory.
Abdullah was sworn in as the chief minister of the Himalayan region on Wednesday.

All senior leaders of the Hurriyat Conference, including Abdul Gani Bhat, Mohamad Yasin Malik, Abdul Gani Lone, Moulana Abbass Ansari, Syed Ali Shah Geelani and Javid Mir were arrested separately in the second and third week of September.
Dozens of separatist groups in Kashmir are fighting for independence or for closer ties with neighbouring Pakistan. They boycotted the polls calling it "a mockery of Kashmiri aspirations".

Pakistan rules one third of the disputed region, called Azad (Free) Kashmir, while India holds the rest. The two nations have fought two of their three wars over Kashmir since independence from Britain in 1947.
More than 20,000 people have been killed since 1990, when the separatist revolt began in Kashmir, hospitals and police sources say.
It was the first government order by Abdullah since he took office, said K.B. Jandial, the state government's official spokesman.
